_format: Sentence tokens are word|role (s=who, v=action/is, o=rest, q=question word, x=helper); _ joins two words into one block. Each lesson needs 3 train, 3 blanks, 2 mistakes (w = index of the wrong word), 2 say.

explain.hi: पास की चीज़ के लिए ‘This is’, दूर की चीज़ के लिए ‘That is’। यह = this, वह = that.
explain.hl: Paas ki cheez ke liye ‘This is’, door ki cheez ke liye ‘That is’. Yeh = this, woh = that.
explain.en: Use ‘This is’ for something near you, and ‘That is’ for something far away.

explain.hi: रंगों को देखो! हिंदी में ‘है’ आख़िर में आता है: यह पेन है। इंग्लिश में ‘is’ बीच में: This is a pen.
explain.hl: Rangon ko dekho! Hindi mein ‘hai’ aakhir mein aata hai: Yeh pen hai. English mein ‘is’ beech mein: This is a pen.
explain.en: Look at the colours! In Hindi, ‘hai’ comes at the end. In English, ‘is’ comes in the middle: This is a pen.

explain.hi: अपने बारे में बोलना हो तो ‘I am’. मैं = I, हूँ = am. जैसे: I am happy = मैं खुश हूँ।
explain.hl: Apne baare mein bolna ho to ‘I am’. Main = I, hoon = am. Jaise: I am happy = Main khush hoon.
explain.en: To talk about yourself, say ‘I am’. Like: I am happy.

explain.hi: ध्यान दो: ‘I’ के साथ हमेशा ‘am’ आता है, कभी ‘is’ नहीं। I is ❌ I am ✅
explain.hl: Dhyaan do: ‘I’ ke saath hamesha ‘am’ aata hai, kabhi ‘is’ nahi. I is ❌ I am ✅
explain.en: Remember: ‘I’ always goes with ‘am’, never ‘is’. I is ❌ I am ✅

explain.hi: लड़के के लिए ‘He’, लड़की के लिए ‘She’, चीज़ या जानवर के लिए ‘It’. तीनों के साथ ‘is’ आता है।
explain.hl: Ladke ke liye ‘He’, ladki ke liye ‘She’, cheez ya jaanwar ke liye ‘It’. Teeno ke saath ‘is’ aata hai.
explain.en: Use ‘He’ for a boy, ‘She’ for a girl, and ‘It’ for a thing or animal. All three go with ‘is’.

explain.hi: हिंदी में ‘वह’ सबके लिए है, पर इंग्लिश में तीन शब्द हैं: He, She, It. ‘लंबा’ या ‘लंबी’ से पता चलता है कौन!
explain.hl: Hindi mein ‘woh’ sabke liye hai, par English mein teen shabd hain: He, She, It. ‘Lamba’ ya ‘lambi’ se pata chalta hai kaun!
explain.en: Hindi uses ‘woh’ for everyone, but English has three words: He, She, It.

blanks.s: Ravi is my friend. ___ is ten.
blanks.hi: रवि मेरा दोस्त है। वह दस साल का है।
blanks.hl: Ravi mera dost hai. Woh das saal ka hai.

blanks.s: Sita is my sister. ___ is kind.
blanks.hi: सीता मेरी बहन है। वह अच्छी है।
blanks.hl: Sita meri behen hai. Woh achhi hai.

blanks.s: This is my dog. ___ is small.
blanks.hi: यह मेरा कुत्ता है। वह छोटा है।
blanks.hl: Yeh mera kutta hai. Woh chhota hai.

explain.hi: एक से ज़्यादा लोग हों, या ‘तुम’ से बात कर रहे हो, तो ‘are’: We are, You are, They are.
explain.hl: Ek se zyaada log hon, ya ‘tum’ se baat kar rahe ho, to ‘are’: We are, You are, They are.
explain.en: For more than one person, or when talking to ‘you’, use ‘are’: We are, You are, They are.

explain.hi: हम = We, तुम = You, वे = They. याद रखो: I am, He/She/It is, बाकी सब are!
explain.hl: Hum = We, tum = You, woh log = They. Yaad rakho: I am, He/She/It is, baaki sab are!
explain.en: Remember: I am, He/She/It is, and all the rest use are!

blanks.hi: तुम मेरे सबसे अच्छे दोस्त हो।
blanks.hl: Tum mere sabse achhe dost ho.

explain.hi: ‘a’ मतलब कोई एक: a book = एक किताब। शब्द a, e, i, o, u की आवाज़ से शुरू हो, तो ‘an’: an apple, an egg.
explain.hl: ‘a’ matlab koi ek: a book = ek kitaab. Shabd a, e, i, o, u ki awaaz se shuru ho, to ‘an’: an apple, an egg.
explain.en: ‘a’ means any one: a book. If the word starts with an a, e, i, o, u sound, use ‘an’: an apple, an egg.

explain.hi: ‘the’ मतलब ‘वो वाला’, जिसकी बात हो रही है: the sun, the book on the table.
explain.hl: ‘the’ matlab ‘woh waala’, jiski baat ho rahi hai: the sun, the book on the table.
explain.en: ‘the’ means one particular thing we both know: the sun, the book on the table.

blanks.hi: मुझे एक कुत्ता दिख रहा है।
blanks.hl: Mujhe ek kutta dikh raha hai.

explain.hi: ‘मेरे पास है’ = I have. ‘उसके पास है’ = He has / She has.
explain.hl: ‘Mere paas hai’ = I have. ‘Uske paas hai’ = He has / She has.
explain.en: Use ‘I have’ for things you own, and ‘He has’ or ‘She has’ for someone else.

explain.hi: हिंदी में ‘है’ आख़िर में आता है। इंग्लिश में: I have a cat — ‘have’ बीच में!
explain.hl: Hindi mein ‘hai’ aakhir mein aata hai. English mein: I have a cat — ‘have’ beech mein!
explain.en: In Hindi, ‘hai’ comes last. In English: I have a cat — ‘have’ goes in the middle!

blanks.hi: उनके पास एक बड़ा घर है।
blanks.hl: Unke paas ek bada ghar hai.

say.hi: उसके पास एक लाल बैग है।
say.hl: Uske paas ek laal bag hai.

explain.hi: ‘मुझे पसंद है’ = I like. जैसे: I like mangoes = मुझे आम पसंद हैं।
explain.hl: ‘Mujhe pasand hai’ = I like. Jaise: I like mangoes = Mujhe aam pasand hain.
explain.en: Say ‘I like’ for things you enjoy: I like mangoes.

explain.hi: हिंदी: मुझे + चीज़ + पसंद है। इंग्लिश: I + like + चीज़। ‘like’ बीच में आता है!
explain.hl: Hindi: mujhe + cheez + pasand hai. English: I + like + cheez. ‘like’ beech mein aata hai!
explain.en: Hindi says the thing first, then ‘pasand hai’. English says: I + like + the thing.

explain.hi: ‘कर सकता हूँ / कर सकती हूँ’ = can. I can swim = मैं तैर सकता हूँ / सकती हूँ।
explain.hl: ‘Kar sakta hoon / kar sakti hoon’ = can. I can swim = Main tair sakta hoon / sakti hoon.
explain.en: Use ‘can’ for things you are able to do: I can swim.

explain.hi: अच्छी बात: ‘can’ कभी नहीं बदलता — I can, he can, she can. और ‘can’ के बाद काम वाला शब्द सीधा आता है: can run.
explain.hl: Achhi baat: ‘can’ kabhi nahi badalta — I can, he can, she can. Aur ‘can’ ke baad kaam waala shabd seedha aata hai: can run.
explain.en: Good news: ‘can’ never changes — I can, he can, she can. And the action word comes straight after it: can run.

explain.hi: किसी जगह कुछ होने की बात: एक चीज़ के लिए ‘There is’, एक से ज़्यादा के लिए ‘There are’।
explain.hl: Kisi jagah kuch hone ki baat: ek cheez ke liye ‘There is’, ek se zyaada ke liye ‘There are’.
explain.en: To say something is somewhere: ‘There is’ for one thing, ‘There are’ for more than one.

explain.hi: मेज़ पर एक किताब है = There is a book on the table. पेड़ पर दो चिड़िया हैं = There are two birds on the tree.
explain.hl: Mez par ek kitaab hai = There is a book on the table. Ped par do chidiya hain = There are two birds on the tree.
explain.en: There is a book on the table. There are two birds on the tree.

train.en: There|s is|v milk|o in|x the|x glass|o

blanks.s: There ___ a dog in the park.
There are two ___ on the tree.

explain.hi: कुछ ढूँढ रहे हो? पूछो: Where is …? = … कहाँ है?
explain.hl: Kuch dhoondh rahe ho? Poochho: Where is …? = … kahan hai?
explain.en: Looking for something? Ask: Where is …?

explain.hi: हिंदी में ‘में, पर, नीचे’ बाद में आते हैं: बैग में। इंग्लिश में पहले: in the bag, on the table, under the bed.
explain.hl: Hindi mein ‘mein, par, neeche’ baad mein aate hain: bag mein. English mein pehle: in the bag, on the table, under the bed.
explain.en: In Hindi, ‘mein, par, neeche’ come after the word. In English, they come before: in the bag, on the table, under the bed.

train.en: The|x pen|s is|v in|o the|x bag|o
The|x cat|s is|v under|o the|x bed|o

mistakes.s: The shoes is under the bed.

say.en: The pen is in the bag.

explain.hi: ‘मुझे चाहिए’ = I want. I want water = मुझे पानी चाहिए।
explain.hl: ‘Mujhe chahiye’ = I want. I want water = Mujhe paani chahiye.
explain.en: Say ‘I want’ when you need or wish for something: I want water.

explain.hi: प्यार से माँगो! आख़िर में ‘please’ लगाओ: I want water, please.
explain.hl: Pyaar se maango! Aakhir mein ‘please’ lagao: I want water, please.
explain.en: Ask nicely! Add ‘please’: I want water, please.

explain.hi: ‘नहीं’ = not. ‘not’ हमेशा am, is, are के बाद आता है: I am not sad.
explain.hl: ‘Nahi’ = not. ‘not’ hamesha am, is, are ke baad aata hai: I am not sad.
explain.en: ‘not’ makes a sentence negative. It comes after am, is, are: I am not sad.

explain.hi: हिंदी: मैं उदास नहीं हूँ। इंग्लिश: I am not sad. ‘not’ बीच में!
explain.hl: Hindi: Main udaas nahi hoon. English: I am not sad. ‘not’ beech mein!
explain.en: Compare: Main udaas nahi hoon = I am not sad. ‘not’ goes in the middle!

explain.hi: सवाल पूछना आसान है! ‘is’ या ‘are’ को आगे ले आओ: It is a cat → Is it a cat?
explain.hl: Sawaal poochna aasaan hai! ‘is’ ya ‘are’ ko aage le aao: It is a cat → Is it a cat?
explain.en: Asking a question is easy! Move ‘is’ or ‘are’ to the front: It is a cat → Is it a cat?

explain.hi: हिंदी में ‘क्या’ लगाते हैं, इंग्लिश में ‘is/are’ आगे आता है। जवाब छोटा दो: Yes, it is. / No, it is not.
explain.hl: Hindi mein ‘kya’ lagaate hain, English mein ‘is/are’ aage aata hai. Jawab chhota do: Yes, it is. / No, it is not.
explain.en: Hindi adds ‘kya’; English moves ‘is/are’ to the front. Give a short answer: Yes, it is. / No, it is not.

blanks.hi: क्या यह गरम है? हाँ, है।
blanks.hl: Kya yeh garam hai? Haan, hai.

explain.hi: क्या = What, कौन = Who, कहाँ = Where. ये सवाल वाले शब्द सबसे आगे आते हैं!
explain.hl: Kya = What, kaun = Who, kahan = Where. Yeh sawaal waale shabd sabse aage aate hain!
explain.en: What, Who and Where are question words. They come first in the question!

explain.hi: हिंदी: तुम्हारा नाम क्या है? इंग्लिश: What is your name? ‘What’ सबसे पहले!
explain.hl: Hindi: Tumhara naam kya hai? English: What is your name? ‘What’ sabse pehle!
explain.en: Compare: Tumhara naam kya hai? = What is your name? ‘What’ comes first!

blanks.hi: तुम्हारा सबसे अच्छा दोस्त कौन है?
blanks.hl: Tumhara sabse achha dost kaun hai?

explain.hi: रोज़ की बातें: I play every day = मैं रोज़ खेलता हूँ / खेलती हूँ।
explain.hl: Roz ki baatein: I play every day = Main roz khelta hoon / khelti hoon.
explain.en: For things you do every day: I play every day.

explain.hi: He, She, It के साथ काम वाले शब्द के आख़िर में ‘s’ लगता है: He plays, She reads. I, We, You, They के साथ नहीं!
explain.hl: He, She, It ke saath kaam waale shabd ke aakhir mein ‘s’ lagta hai: He plays, She reads. I, We, You, They ke saath nahi!
explain.en: With He, She and It, add ‘s’ to the action word: He plays, She reads. Not with I, We, You, They!

blanks.hi: मैं रोज़ सुबह दाँत साफ़ करती हूँ।
blanks.hl: Main roz subah daant saaf karti hoon.

mistakes.hi: वह अपनी गुड़िया से खेलती है।
mistakes.hl: Woh apni gudiya se khelti hai.

say.en: I go to school every day.
